div.p: I have everything I need. Here's the full audit:

hr.p: 1. Site not indexed by Google A site:aidashbd.com search returns zero results. Google either hasn't crawled the site or has excluded it entirely. This means the site is essentially invisible in search right now.
2. No robots.txt aidashbd.com/robots.txt returns a 404 error. Without this file, search engines don't know what to crawl. It also suggests the site has no crawl configuration at all.
3. No sitemap.xml aidashbd.com/sitemap.xml also returns a 404. A sitemap tells Google which pages exist and helps it index the site faster. This is especially important for new sites.

4. HTTP — no HTTPS The site loads on http:// not https://. Google officially uses HTTPS as a ranking signal. Browsers also show a "Not Secure" warning, which damages visitor trust. GitHub Pages supports free HTTPS — enable it in the repo settings.

5. Thin content on every listing Each AI tool only shows a name, category tags, traffic number, and a rating. There's no description, no review, no use cases — nothing original. Google values unique, useful content. Right now the site is just a link directory, which ranks very poorly.

6. No meta title or meta description visible From the fetched source, there are no distinguishable <title> or <meta name="description"> tags in the markup. These are among the most important on-page SEO elements. Without them, Google will auto-generate something arbitrary for search results.

7. No individual pages per tool All 183 tools are displayed on a single page. Search engines can't rank individual tools when they have no unique URL. A page like /tool/chatgpt with its own title, description, and content would be far more rankable than a card in a long list.

8. Animated GIF as logo The logo (aidashbd.gif) is a GIF file. GIFs are large and slow to load. Replace it with an optimized SVG or WebP image and add a proper alt attribute for accessibility and image SEO.

9. No structured data (Schema markup) Adding ItemList or SoftwareApplication schema would help Google understand this is a directory of AI tools, and could enable rich results (star ratings, app info) in search.
10. Emojis in navigation Navigation items like "💬 Chat AI" and "🎨 Image AI" rely on emojis. Search engines can read these but they don't add keyword value. Text-only labels are cleaner for SEO.

11. No heading hierarchy The page uses H1 for the site name ("AI-DASHBD") but there's no logical H2/H3 structure for categories or tools. Proper heading hierarchy helps Google understand page structure.

12. All outbound links are untracked redirects Links go through tool.html?slug=... before sending users to affiliate destinations. Make sure these links have rel="nofollow sponsored" tags — Google requires this for affiliate/paid links, otherwise it may penalize the site for unnatural link schemes.

13. No Open Graph or Twitter Card tags When anyone shares a link to this site on social media, it shows no image, no title, no description — just a blank preview. This kills click-through rates from social sharing.

ul.li: Affiliate disclosure notice at the top is good — legally required and Google-friendly
The category filter/sort system gives users a good experience
Internal routing via tool.html?slug= keeps users on-site before redirecting

tr.td: Submit site to Google Search Console
Add a short description to each AI tool card
Create individual pages per tool with unique content
Add rel="nofollow sponsored" to all affiliate links
Add Open Graph / Twitter Card meta tags
Clean up emoji navigation for plain text

hr.p: The single biggest opportunity is creating individual pages for each AI tool with original descriptions and use cases. That alone could transform the site from an invisible link list into something Google actively ranks. Would you like help building any of these improvements?
